SMTO-SCH-0011 — An edited schedule can't take on new private values

GUID: df0452aa-bcea-400c-963a-ffacb84a3f52
Slug: schedule-private-context-rejected
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • You changed a saved schedule's text so that it types in a value or uses a saved password. Edits can't add private values to a schedule, so the change wasn't saved and the schedule still has its old text.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the schedule editor, remove any typein "..." text or any mention of using a saved password or value from the Parameter Store, then select Save changes. An existing schedule keeps the private values it was created with and can't gain new ones through an edit.
  2. If the schedule really needs a different private value, create a new schedule from a conversation instead. A new schedule goes through the normal setup that handles private values safely.
  3. Then pause or delete the old schedule on the Schedules page so both don't run. This avoids the same work running twice from two schedules.

What success looks like

  • The edit saves, or the new schedule appears on the Schedules page and the old one shows as paused or is gone.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the password or secret itself into the schedule text.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A scope-preserving schedule edit was rejected because the new title, prompt or notification text parses as private macro content (typein, Parameter Store or sudo-password references) that would add or replace private execution context.

What this means

  • A scope-preserving schedule edit parses the new prompt and detects macros that would add or replace private execution context. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • A scope-preserving schedule edit parses the new prompt and detects macros that would add or replace private execution context.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the edited prompt with the existing captured scope and macro-free edit contract.

How to fix it

  • Remove the macro syntax from the edited title/prompt/notification_message (events/management.py ScheduleManagementService.update). If the schedule genuinely needs different private context, create a new schedule through the normal preparation flow and pause or delete the old one, keeping its run history.
  • Create a new schedule through the supported preparation flow if its private macro context must change. Preserve the existing schedule history.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A permitted edit preserves scope, or a deliberate new schedule captures its own authorized context.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
